guides.name: Plumbing
guides.summary: Most small plumbing jobs cost £75–£150, typically about £100, done in one visit.
guides.rates: £40–£60 per hour (typical £50), £320–£480 per day. Emergency and out-of-hours work runs £75–£150 per hour, often with a £100–£120 call-out.

jobs.name: Fix a leak (pipe, tap or under the sink)
Unblock a sink, bath, shower or toilet
Fix a running or leaking toilet
Replace a kitchen or bathroom tap (labour)

guides.included: Labour, travel within the area, small fittings (washers, olives, PTFE), testing the repair for leaks, taking away old parts.
guides.notIncluded: New taps, toilets, showers or radiators unless agreed; re-tiling or re-plastering after access; any gas work (needs a Gas Safe engineer).

raisers.label: Pipes hidden behind tiles, boxing or floors
Old lead, iron or corroded pipework that needs more replacing
Parts that cost more than standard

guides.name: Electrician
guides.summary: Most small electrical jobs cost £55–£150, typically about £65–£100.
guides.rates: About £45–£65 per hour (typical £55), around £500 per day. Emergency work is about £90 per hour.

jobs.name: Replace a socket or light switch
Find and fix a tripping fuse

guides.included: Labour, testing after the work, small consumables, and a certificate for notifiable work (Part P).
guides.notIncluded: The fitting, fan or fuse box itself; making good plaster or paint after chasing cables.

raisers.label: Old wiring with no earth, or work that fails testing
Fault-finding that takes longer than an hour
New circuits or cable runs instead of a like-for-like swap
High ceilings that need a tower or extra ladder work

guides.name: Cleaning
guides.summary: A regular clean is about £25 an hour; an end-of-tenancy clean is £180–£415 depending on size.
guides.rates: £20–£30 per hour (typical £25). Agencies sit at the top of the range.
guides.included: Cleaning products and equipment, kitchen surfaces and appliances outside, bathrooms, dusting, hoovering and mopping.
guides.notIncluded: Outside windows, carpet shampooing, laundry and ironing, taking away rubbish.

raisers.label: Heavy grease, limescale, mould or a home left in poor condition
Pets and pet hair
Extra rooms, inside fridges and cupboards, or balconies

guides.name: Carpets
guides.summary: Carpet cleaning starts at about £50 a room, often with an £85 minimum per visit. Fitting is about £8–£12 per m² for labour and underlay.
guides.rates: Fitters charge £20–£35 per hour or £150–£250 per day; cleaning firms £60–£120 per hour.

jobs.name: Clean a small room (4 m × 4 m)
Fit carpet with underlay (labour and underlay)
Carpet a standard bedroom (carpet supplied by fitter)

guides.included: Cleaning: pre-treatment of normal marks and drying advice. Fitting: gripper, fitting, trimming and taking away offcuts.
guides.notIncluded: The carpet itself (unless quoted), lifting and disposing of old carpet, moving heavy furniture, floor levelling.

raisers.label: Old stains, pet urine or heavy soiling
Winding or open-plan staircases
Uneven floors that need levelling or new gripper
Patterned carpet that needs matching

guides.name: Painting and decorating
guides.summary: Painting a medium room costs about £350–£550, typically £450. Decorators charge £250–£350 a day.

jobs.name: Paint one room, walls and ceiling
Paint skirting and a door in one room

guides.included: Preparation (filling small cracks, sanding, masking, dust sheets), two coats, clearing up.
guides.notIncluded: Paint and wallpaper unless agreed, stripping old wallpaper, plaster repairs bigger than small cracks, moving heavy furniture.

raisers.label: High ceilings and stairwells that need a platform
Going from a dark colour to a light one (extra coats)
Stripping wallpaper or treating damp and stains first
Lots of woodwork, spindles or detailed mouldings

guides.name: Handyman
guides.summary: Most handyman jobs take one to four hours and cost £45–£200. Many charge a one-hour minimum.

jobs.name: Put up a curtain pole or blind
Mount a TV on the wall (bracket supplied)
Put up 8 shelves in a living room
Half a day of odd jobs

guides.included: Labour, standard screws, plugs and fixings, tidying up.
guides.notIncluded: The item being fitted (TV bracket, shelves, blinds), work that legally needs a qualified electrician or Gas Safe engineer.

raisers.label: Hard or hollow walls that need special fixings
Large or complex flat-pack (wardrobes, beds with storage)
Work at height
Parking charges or congestion zones

guides.name: Carpentry
guides.summary: Small carpentry repairs cost about £45–£150; hanging a new internal door costs £125–£350 including a basic door.
guides.rates: About £30–£45 per hour, £200–£300 per day (Fixmet estimate).

jobs.name: Ease a sticking or dropped door
Hang an internal door (softwood door included)
Hang an internal door (hardwood door included)
Fit new skirting in one room

guides.included: Labour, fixings, hinges and handles reused, clearing offcuts.
guides.notIncluded: New doors, timber or ironmongery unless quoted; painting or staining afterwards.

raisers.label: Out-of-square frames or uneven floors
Fire doors, which need certified fitting
Rotten timber found once work starts
Bespoke sizes that need cutting or building to measure

guides.name: Builder
guides.summary: Builders usually price by the day: about £250–£350 for a builder, £120–£280 for a labourer. Small repairs are £150–£800.
guides.rates: Builder about £300 per day; bricklayer £250–£350; labourer £120–£280.

jobs.name: Patch plaster on a wall (small area)
Repair a section of garden wall
Repoint the front of a house

guides.included: Labour, sand and cement for small repairs, clearing the work area.
guides.notIncluded: Scaffolding (£15–£25 per m²), skip hire, matching bricks or stone, building control fees.

raisers.label: Scaffolding or access towers
Raking out old mortar before repointing
Matching reclaimed or period bricks
Hidden problems such as failed foundations or damp

guides.name: Roofer
guides.summary: Small roof repairs usually cost £150–£500. Larger repairs are priced per m² or per metre, and access equipment is extra.

jobs.name: Replace a few slipped tiles (ladder access)
Find and repair a roof leak
Patch a flat roof (felt, rubber or GRP)

guides.included: Labour, matching tiles or slates for small areas, fixings, taking away broken tiles.
guides.notIncluded: Scaffolding or access towers, full strip-and-replace, VAT, internal repairs to ceilings.

raisers.label: Scaffolding or a cherry picker
Steep or high roofs, and three-storey houses
Rotten battens or felt found under the tiles
Rare or reclaimed tiles that are hard to match

guides.name: Gutters
guides.summary: Gutter cleaning costs about £50–£120 for a small terraced house, rising to £130–£165 for a detached house.

jobs.name: Clean gutters, small terraced house (about 5 m)

guides.included: Removing leaves, moss and debris; clearing downpipes; flushing to check flow; taking waste away; pointing out visible damage.
guides.notIncluded: Repairs found during cleaning, new parts, scaffolding or a cherry picker for complex jobs.

raisers.label: Heavily blocked gutters or plants growing in them
Height, conservatories or extensions in the way
Blocked downpipes that need rodding
Cast-iron gutters

guides.name: Window cleaning
guides.summary: Outside window cleaning costs about £30–£40 per visit for most houses.
guides.rates: About £20–£30 per hour. Regular customers on a 4–8 week round pay less per visit than one-off cleans.

jobs.name: Outside only, terraced house or bungalow

guides.included: Glass, frames and sills on the outside; pure-water pole or ladder.
guides.notIncluded: Inside windows unless booked, conservatory roofs, gutters and fascias.

raisers.label: A one-off clean instead of a regular round
Windows above second floor, or no rear access
Very dirty glass after building work (paint, cement)
Lots of small panes such as Georgian or leaded windows

guides.name: Patio care
guides.summary: Pressure-washing a patio costs about £2–£5 per m², so a typical 20 m² patio is £60–£100 once a minimum charge applies. Cleaning and sealing roughly doubles it.
guides.included: Pressure washing, moss and weed removal from joints, rinsing away debris.
guides.notIncluded: Sealant (unless booked), re-sanding block paving, replacing cracked slabs, water if the customer has no outside tap.

raisers.label: Heavy moss, algae or oil stains needing chemical treatment
Re-sanding block paving after washing
No outside tap or no drainage
Steps, walls and edging on top of the flat area

guides.name: Gardening
guides.summary: Gardeners charge about £20–£35 an hour, so most one-off tidy-ups cost £50–£200.
guides.rates: £20–£35 per hour (typical £27.50), £160–£260 per day. Landscape gardeners charge £180–£330 per day.

jobs.name: Mow and edge a small lawn

guides.included: Labour, the gardener's own mower, trimmers and hand tools, bagging cuttings.
guides.notIncluded: Taking green waste away (often £60+ per load), plants, turf, compost and skip hire.

raisers.label: Overgrown gardens left for a season or more
Green waste removal and tip fees
Tall hedges that need platforms or climbing gear
No side access, so everything goes through the house

guides.name: Movers and removals
guides.summary: A local move with two people and a van costs about £50–£80 an hour. A full move is roughly £450 for 1 bedroom up to £1,200 for 4 bedrooms, before packing.
guides.rates: £50–£80 per hour for two movers and a van; packers about £35 per hour.

jobs.name: Man and van, a few items (2 hours)

guides.included: Loading, transport, unloading into the right rooms, blankets and straps, basic goods-in-transit cover.
guides.notIncluded: Packing and boxes, dismantling furniture, storage, parking permits, long-distance fuel.

raisers.label: Stairs with no lift, or long carries from the van
Pianos, safes and other heavy items
Long distances or congestion and ULEZ charges
Weekends, bank holidays and month-end dates

guides.name: Fire safety
guides.summary: Fitting a battery smoke alarm costs about £25–£75; mains-wired alarms are £150–£250 each. A fire risk assessment for a small building starts at about £150.
guides.rates: Mains-wired work is priced at electrician rates (£45–£65 per hour).

jobs.name: Fit a battery smoke or heat alarm
Grade A alarm system (HMO or block)

guides.included: Fitting, testing, and a certificate for mains-wired and Grade A systems.
guides.notIncluded: The alarms unless quoted, making good after cabling, annual servicing.

raisers.label: Mains wiring where there is no nearby circuit
HMOs, flats and commercial buildings that need a full system
Interlinking several alarms
Reports needed urgently for a letting or insurance deadline
